labels.label: bzprop:c3s3p1_dualite_biunivoque

hypotheses.paper: E, E' semi-reflexive TVS « mis en dualité »
hypotheses.note: prop1 under HypD (each space the topological dual of the other through the form: the dual-pair reading the proof uses); prop1_semiReflexive under 'E semi-reflexive (IsSemiReflexive, Bourbaki), E' = E'_beta its strong dual'

findings: Props. 1 and 2 2° (benzecri1960_ch3.tex:685-690, 698-702) fail if « mis en dualité » / « les hypothèses de (d) » mean only a separating, separately continuous form between semi-reflexive spaces carrying their own topologies (argued on paper, not formalized): on l² (reflexive), <x,y> = (x|Ty) with T = diag(1/n) (injective, self-adjoint, dense non-closed range) is separating and jointly continuous; for z = (1/n) ∉ T(l²) and W the closed hemisphere {(x|z) ≥ 0}, D(W) = s{y≠0 | Ty ∈ R+ z} = ∅ = D(S(l²)) with W ≠ S(l²), both in C(S(l²)), so D is not injective (Prop. 1) and D'(D(W)) = S(l²) ≠ W̄ (Prop. 2 2°). No finite-dimensional counterexample exists (a separating form is then perfect). Both hold, and are proved (prop1, prop1_semiReflexive, prop2_2), under the dual-pair reading the proofs use (each space the topological dual of the other through the form). The zero form (prop1_fails_zeroForm) refutes only a degenerate « dualité », which the Bourbaki of the period (EVT 1955) probably excludes; it is a remark, not a refutation of the paper.
questions: What « deux espaces vectoriels topologiques semi-réflexifs mis en dualité » means (l.686): taken as the hypotheses of (d) (prop1), and alternatively as 'E semi-reflexive, E' its strong dual' (prop1_semiReflexive). Neither is the printed sentence; the author decides which is the formalization of record.
